seo_description:
Full-court 1v1 with change-of-direction read after midline touch.
Main Goal
Train change-of-pace and change-of-direction decisions for the ball-handler while developing defensive reaction speed, recovery angles, and containment in open space.
Setup
1. One ball-handler (O1) and one defender (X1) start next to each other behind the baseline. O1 has the ball.
2. At the opposite half (midcourt), two cones form a small gate on the midline. Both players must run forward and touch the midline (at least one foot on or beyond it).

phases.notes: The drill starts when the ball-handler moves. The defender can react immediately and sprint as well.
phases.title: Phase 1

content.text: The drill starts when the ball-handler moves. The defender can react immediately and sprint as well.

phases.notes:
1. After touching the midline, the ball-handler can decide: continue forward and attack the far basket OR plant, change direction, and attack back to the original basket.
2. The defender must read the offensive decision, adjust angles, and defend live until the layup attempt.

3. Time pressure: Shot must occur within 4 seconds after the midline touch.
4. Progression: Allow defender to start half a step ahead to increase pressure and force more decisive change-of-direction moves.

Main Goal
Develop agility, awareness, and ball control as players react to a moving chaser and a teammate creating protection through body positioning.
Setup
Define a playing area, for example the paint.
Assign three roles: a dog (chaser), a rabbit (runner), and a farmer (protector).
The dog starts with a ball. All three players start inside the area.

seo_description:
Chase, evade, and sprint back in a race against the clock.
Main Goal
Prepare players for practice through quick reactions, changes of direction, and repeated sprints in a competitive team game.
Setup
1. Divide players into two equal teams: runners (X) and taggers (O).
2. Define the playing area, for example the half court.
3. The runners spread out inside the area. The taggers line up behind the baseline.

phases.title: Phase 4

content.text: Tagged runners stay in the playing area and continue moving. They can be tagged again by a different tagger.

phases.notes:
Continue until every tagger has tagged a runner and returned behind the baseline. Stop the clock when the final tagger crosses the line.
Switch roles and repeat under the same conditions. The team with the faster total time wins.

2. Dribbling runners: Give every runner a ball. Runners must maintain their dribble while avoiding the tagger.
3. Everyone dribbles: Give the taggers a ball as well. They must dribble while chasing and returning to the baseline, tagging with their free hand.

seo_description:
Read the closeout and choose between the shot and the drive.
Main Goal
Help offensive players recognize an open shot or attack a closeout, then adjust their finish to the defender protecting the basket.
Setup
1. Two defenders (X1 and X2) stand facing each other inside the three-point line, with one ball between them.
2. One offensive player (O1) starts outside the three-point line, between the defenders’ positions.

cached_payload.title: Shoot or Drive: Two-Defender Read

phases.notes: X1 and X2 pass the ball back and forth.
phases.title: Phase 1

content.text: X1 and X2 pass the ball back and forth.

phases.notes:
1. Either defender can choose when to pass to O1, keeping the timing and direction of the entry pass unpredictable.
2. As soon as a defender passes to O1, that defender drops under the basket. The other defender closes out to contest the shot.
phases.title: Phase 2

content.text: Either defender can choose when to pass to O1, keeping the timing and direction of the entry pass unpredictable.
As soon as a defender passes to O1, that defender drops under the basket. The other defender closes out to contest the shot.

phases.notes: O1 reads the closeout and decides whether to shoot or attack the basket. If the closeout arrives late, O1 looks to take the open shot.
phases.title: Phase 3

content.text: O1 reads the closeout and decides whether to shoot or attack the basket. If the closeout arrives late, O1 looks to take the open shot.

phases.notes:
If the defender closes out aggressively, O1 can drive past and finish against the defender under the rim.
Play until a score, defensive rebound, or turnover. Reset and rotate roles so each player gets repetitions as the shooter and both defenders.
Constraints
1. Stationary rim defender: Once the passer reaches the position under the basket, they must keep their feet planted and may only contest with their arms — no jumping or moving to challenge the drive.
2. Reward the shot: Award 3 points for a made shot and 1 point for a basket off the drive.
3. Reward the drive: Reverse the scoring emphasis: 3 points for a basket off the drive and 1 point for a made shot. Choose one scoring system based on the practice focus.

seo_description:
Quick reactions, agility, and evasion under pressure.
Main Goal
Improve first-step quickness and evasive movement while training the defender to react explosively and protect space.
Setup
1. One offensive player (the runner) starts on the baseline.
2. A defender (the tagger) stands at the free-throw line, holding a ball with both hands.
3. Two cones are placed to the left and right of the defender.

cached_payload.title: Tag & Escape Warm-Up (1v1)

phases.notes:
1. The drill begins when the runner initiates movement. The runner must try to reach either cone without being tagged by the tagger’s ball.
2. The tagger may only tag using the ball held with two hands — no reaching or swinging with arms allowed.
phases.title: Phase 1

content.text: The drill begins when the runner initiates movement. The runner must try to reach either cone without being tagged by the tagger’s ball.
The tagger may only tag using the ball held with two hands — no reaching or swinging with arms allowed.

3. Move the tagger’s starting position (wider, narrower, angled).
4. The runner must perform at least one cross over (behind the back / between the legs).
